transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you. Um, is it okay if I sit right here? ... Okay, thank you. 

Well, I'm here because... I guess I've just been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. I drive for a living, and I really don't want to sound like a difficult employee or a complainer, because I know management has a job to do, but... dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes. 

They do it through the computer system, and they make these little comments on the radio. And, you know, when I try to talk about it, people say it’s just normal oversight. Which I really try to accept! I know they have to monitor us. But... I can just tell that certain other drivers are reporting on me. 

I hope I'm explaining that okay. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.

Have you generally been a suspicious or distrustful person for most of your life, or is this feeling of being watched and reported on something that started more recently and feels different from how you used to think?

Oh, no, definitely not my whole life. I actually... I really pride myself on being a very trusting person. I always try to be a good team player and get along with everyone at the depot. I really don't want you to think I'm just, um, a naturally suspicious person who looks for things to complain about, because I promise I'm not. 

It's just... this specific thing, with the tracking on the computer and those little comments on the radio? It really just started recently. I'd say it's felt really clear to me for about the past two months. Before that, everything was totally fine and I loved my routes. 

Um, is that what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not rambling too much.

When you hear those comments on the radio, are you certain other people around you are hearing the exact same thing, or do you ever notice that others don't seem to hear or notice what you're hearing?

Um, well... that's a really good question. I guess... since I'm driving, I'm usually by myself in the cab, you know? So there isn't really anyone else sitting right next to me to ask if they heard it too. 

And, um, when I am back at the depot or if I'm around the other drivers, I... I haven't really asked anyone else if they notice the comments. I really don't want to seem difficult or make my coworkers uncomfortable by bringing it up, and I definitely don't want to cause any drama. I just try to keep my head down and be a good employee, so I usually just let it go. 

So I'm actually not totally sure if they hear the exact same things or not. I'm sorry, I hope that's an okay answer? I just haven't really checked with anyone else to see if they notice it.

When you hear those comments about you on the radio, are you hearing actual words or voices that come through the radio, or do you think it's more that you're interpreting normal radio chatter or static as being about you?

Um, well... I mean, I definitely hear words. Like, actual words. But I know radios can be staticky and, you know, sometimes it's hard to hear perfectly. 

I really don't want you to think I'm making things up or imagining voices out of nowhere, because I promise I'm not doing that. It's just... when the dispatchers are talking, or the other drivers are checking in, I can hear them saying things about my route, or about me. It sounds like regular radio talk, just... the words are about me. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound weirder than it is. I know it sounds a little strange when I say it out loud, but I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer.

Besides these experiences with the radio and being watched, have you noticed any other changes lately—like trouble concentrating, your thoughts feeling jumbled, seeing or sensing things that others don't, or difficulty keeping up with your usual daily routine and responsibilities?

Um, well... I really try my best to keep everything running smoothly, I promise. I'm usually very organized. But, um... I guess lately, things have been just a little bit harder to keep up with. 

I don't want to sound like I'm not doing my job, because I really am trying, but... I've fallen a bit behind on my route reports. And, um, sometimes the instructions I give the drivers... I guess they've been a little confusing? A few of them have complained, which makes me feel awful because I always want to be helpful. 

And then at home... I really hate to admit this, because I like taking care of things, but my husband has had to step in a lot more. He's been doing the cooking and handling phone calls and just... figuring out the basic planning for the week. I just haven't been keeping up the way I usually do. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or incapable, because I'm really not. I'm just... having a little trouble right now. Is it okay that I'm telling you all this? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.

Have these experiences with the radio comments and feeling watched been happening continuously every day for the past two months, or do they come and go with periods where you feel completely back to normal?

Um, well... I really don't want to make it sound like I'm complaining or that I can't handle my job, because I really do try to just push through it. But, um... it hasn't really gone away. 

I guess... for about the past two months, it's been pretty constant. The feeling that they're tracking me through the computer system, and the things I hear on the radio... it's just been really clear to me every day. There haven't really been breaks where I feel totally normal again, even though I wish there were. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably isn't the best thing to hear, and I really hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it. I just want to be honest with you so you can help. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?

Over these past two months, have you also noticed significant changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or empty most of the day, or on the other hand, feeling unusually energetic, elated, or needing much less sleep than usual?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I really try to stay positive, you know? I don't want to bring anyone down. So, no, I haven't been feeling super sad or hopeless or anything like that. I'm definitely not crying all day or feeling empty. 

And I'm definitely not, like, bouncing off the walls or staying up all night either. I know sleep is really important for doing a good job at work, so I always make sure I try to get enough rest. My energy is just... normal, I guess? 

I really hope that's okay. I'm just trying to be as helpful as I can. I don't want to make things seem worse than they are, but I also want to make sure I'm giving you the right details. Did I answer that okay?
Since these experiences started about two months ago and have been continuous, do you have any sense of whether they've been getting better, worse, or staying about the same over that time?

Um, well... I'd really like to say they're getting better. I've been trying so hard to just focus on my work and be a good employee, you know? But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... they haven't really improved. 

I don't think they're getting a lot worse, though! I'm still managing, I promise. It's just... it's just stayed about the same, I think. The radio and the feeling of the computer tracking me, it's just sort of... always there, at the same level. 

I hope it's not disappointing that I haven't been able to make it go away on my own. I really have been trying. Is it normal for things to just stay the same like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.

Before these past two months when the radio comments and tracking feelings became clear, did you notice any earlier changes—even subtle ones, like feeling a bit off, more withdrawn, or having unusual thoughts—going back further, say four to six months ago?

Um, well... I really don't want you to think I couldn't handle the responsibility, because I was actually really honored when they asked me. But, um... I guess if I think back, things might have started feeling a little off before these last two months. 

I've been trying so hard to just do a good job, but... maybe about eight months ago? That's when they put me in a temporary dispatch lead role. It was a great opportunity, I promise, and I was so grateful they trusted me with it! But... I guess that's when I started feeling, um, just a little different. Like things were sort of building up from there. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm complaining about the promotion or that I'm ungrateful. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. Is it helpful to know about the promotion?

When you say things started feeling 'a little different' around the time of that promotion 8 months ago, can you tell me more specifically what that felt like—was it more just stress or worry about the new role, or did you notice any early versions of these same kinds of experiences, like feeling watched or suspicious of others, even in a milder way?

Um, oh, no, it wasn't anything like feeling watched or being suspicious of anyone back then. I would never want to think bad things about my team, they're really great people. 

I think... I think it was really just normal stress about the new role. I just wanted so badly to do a perfect job, you know? To prove that they made the right choice in picking me. So I was just, um, worrying a lot more than usual. Just really overthinking my work and making sure I didn't mess up any of the schedules. 

The things with the radio and the computer, that definitely wasn't happening back then. It was just me putting a lot of pressure on myself to be a good lead. I hope that's okay? I mean, I hope that's the kind of information you're looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline for everything.

Going back to when the stress and overthinking started about 8 months ago, did you notice any continuous change in how you were functioning day-to-day since then—like becoming more withdrawn from friends or family, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy—that has persisted up through today?

Um... well, please don't think I'm just being lazy or that I don't care about my friends, because I really do. I don't want to sound like a bad person. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, I have stepped back a little bit. 

I just haven't really felt like... well, like singing with the choir lately, or having the softball team over to my place like I used to. I've been trying to tell myself I'm just saving my energy so I can do a good job at work, you know? But it's gotten to where most days, after my shift, I just go home and sit at the kitchen table. 

I always have my planner open right in front of me, because I really do want to be productive and stay on top of things! But I just sort of sit there. I can't seem to make myself actually start making dinner, or return phone calls, or do much of anything else. 

I feel awful about it, I really do. I keep meaning to do better. Is it normal to get that drained when you're stressed? I hope I'm explaining this the right way... I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
